findings.reason: the plan should cite this module as the cost owner and route its decision through it, which removes a measurement work item and a duplicate implementation path.
findings.text: §3 states "Cost per identity — measured, not estimated: compose is free on the local seat and review is the paid axis, and the figure is dominated by quorum draws" and the followup asks a worker to measure it, but `campaign_pricing.py` already renders the production review request for every identity and prices the complete reviewer chain (first two seats mandatory, third as worst-case escalation) with no model call — the plan would re-derive a figure an existing module computes

findings.reason: if source-refresh already refreshes stale docs, the freshness benefit §2 prices may be partly banked, which changes the threshold the plan must state.
findings.text: §2 treats "stale generated documentation" as what "regeneration is actually for", but `source_refresh.py` already re-refines existing names when their DD source drifts (effective unit/documentation/path change steers an `axis='docs'` refine, idempotent on re-run) and the pipeline already re-refines docs without a delete-and-rebuild

findings.reason: the prerequisite plan already owns provenance recovery, so the finding sharpens the citation rather than changing the scope decision.
findings.text: §2's residue table ("dual-bound source with a single-producer loser", "recoverable link topology", "unresolved residue") is the same reasoning `provenance_rebuild.py` already encodes, which replays "the deterministic half of a fresh build against the existing names — it never regenerates names or docs" — the plan cites none of it

findings.reason: extending the origin-query owner keeps one population definition and prevents the plan's census from drifting from the pricing cohort it must match.
findings.text: the regenerable/protected population counts are graph queries over `origin` (`AND sn.origin = 'catalog_edit'` here, alongside `coverage`/`status` in `imas_codex/cli/sn.py`), and the plan would measure them ad hoc as raw counts (`2,096`, `2,031`, `1,099`) instead of extending the owner that already queries origin for pricing

findings.reason: naming the existing guard as the enforcement point turns "must exclude" from a plan assertion into an existing invariant the regenerate can lean on.
findings.text: §3's "Protected population ... which a regenerate must exclude rather than rebuild" restates the protection mechanism `protection.py` already owns (`PROTECTED_FIELDS`, `filter_protected()`), which every protected-field writer already calls

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new module; its work is a census plus a decision, so there is no interface spreading complexity across wrappers to judge.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's "cost per identity" and "regenerable/protected population" duplicates owners `imas_codex/standard_names/campaign_pricing.py` and `imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py`, and its documentation-regeneration scope duplicates `imas_codex/standard_names/source_refresh.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the plan adds no public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family; public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 are unchanged, and the only new surface is a plan decision block (`regenerate-scope`) which is not one of the four families.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched no codebase: cost-per-identity is already priced by `imas_codex/standard_names/campaign_pricing.py`, documentation regeneration by `imas_codex/standard_names/source_refresh.py`, and deterministic rebuild-vs-residue reasoning by `imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_rebuild.py`, and §3 lists all of these as quantities still to be measured rather than mechanisms to extend.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no wrapper layer over existing machinery; it either extends the pipeline (regenerate) or does not, and no thin wrapper is proposed.
